symbols.note: copied from `gatekit symbols system <name> --dll dx11 --full` (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe; methods without an address were not found in the game binary and are listed with address null). Parsed by script from the command output, not retyped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Runs when a FrameworkReloadRequestOneFrameComponent has appeared this frame. The request entities are destroyed. If the framework object is already loaded, it serialises the state of every Anubis tree entity (those with AnubisTree, Config and Tree) and adds ls::anubis::savegame::ReloadingComponent, carrying that state, to the helper entity; if the framework is not loaded, it adds ls::anubis::ReinitializingComponent to that helper entity instead. It also removes ErrorComponent from every entity that has one. When the reload is finished it removes Reinitializing or Reloading again and adds a one-frame FrameworkReloadedOneFrameComponent.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll (Toolkit build, named) ls::anubis::System::ProcessReloadRequests +0x796D0 = bg3_dx11.exe+0x382C660, read as pseudo-code in slices. Component types behind the DAT_ type-index globals were resolved from the GetTypeName strings of their initialisers (query Spec added-list = FrameworkReloadRequest; adders at AnubisFramework.dll+0x4D490 -> Reloading, +0x4D2A0 -> Reinitializing, +0x4C5E0 -> FrameworkReloaded; each of the three adders calls SetupComponentFrameStorage, so they add). The 'framework loaded' test is a helper returning whether the framework object pointer at +0xC0 is non-null (AnubisFramework.dll+0xE25E0); that this is the guard of the Reloading branch is my reading of the control flow.

does.text: If a FrameworkUnloadRequestOneFrameComponent has appeared this frame, it tells the framework object to drop everything it holds: the event storage is emptied, the tree storage is emptied and one more framework-side container is reset. It adds and removes no component.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll ls::anubis::System::ProcessUnloadRequests +0x7BFE0 (60 lines, read whole); the helper it calls at AnubisFramework.dll+0xE3FF0 calls EventStorage::RemoveAll and TreeStorage::RemoveAll. Query Spec resolved to FrameworkUnloadRequestOneFrameComponent.

does.text: For each EditorChangeOneFrameComponent that appeared this frame the system notes the entity it concerns in a set; then for tree entities that also gained the constellation component it looks them up in that set and asks the framework to run the constellation tree's editor-changes callback. It adds or removes no component.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll ls::anubis::System::ProcessEditorChanges +0x75A60 (read in slices; no AddComponent/RemoveComponent/DestroyEntity in the body); callee AnubisFramework.dll+0xE1960 constructs a ConstellationTreeRef and calls CallOnEditorChanges. Queries resolved to EditorChangeOneFrameComponent added, and TreeComponent + constellation::Component added.

does.text: Two loops over tree entities: those with a CreateEditorPreviewVisualRequestOneFrameComponent this frame make the framework call the tree's OnCreateEditorPreviewVisual callback; those with a DestroyEditorPreviewVisualRequestOneFrameComponent make it call OnDestroyEditorPreviewVisual. No component is added or removed.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll ls::anubis::System::ProcessEditorPreviewVisualEvents +0x76180; no component add/remove calls in the body; callees AnubisFramework.dll+0xE18E0 and +0xE1920 call ConstellationTreeRef::CallOnCreateEditorPreviewVisual / CallOnDestroyEditorPreviewVisual. Query Specs resolved to the Create and Destroy request components.

does.text: For tree entities that got a DebuggingActivatedOneFrameComponent this frame it builds a debug TreeView of the tree through the framework and adds ls::anubis::debug::TreeViewBuiltOneFrameComponent carrying it; unless the entity was also marked deactivated in the same frame it also adds HistoryComponent. For entities that received DebuggingDeactivatedOneFrameComponent it removes HistoryComponent.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll ls::anubis::System::ProcessDebugComponents +0x75260. Adders: AnubisFramework.dll+0x4E3A0 uses the type index of TreeViewBuiltOneFrame (resolved), +0x4C9C0 that of HistoryComponent, both through SetupComponentFrameStorage; RemoveComponentUnchecked with the HistoryComponent index at the end. Which branch decides between adding HistoryComponent or not (a hash-set lookup of entities deactivated this frame) is read from control flow only.

does.text: Three jobs. (1) For tree entities with ScriptCmdSaveAnubisStateOneFrameComponent it serialises the tree state (for StateComponent, resolved as the written type; the exact add of it was not read). (2) For entities that already have StateComponent and Config and got a ScriptCmdRestoreAnubisStateOneFrameComponent, it checks the saved state holds exactly one tree at index 0 and one component, asks ConfigSystem to change the entity's config, and adds RestoringStateComponent (with the saved data) and WaitingForConfigChangeComponent. (3) WaitingForConfigChange is removed once the config has changed; when an entity has RestoringState, a Tree and no WaitingForConfigChange any more, the saved state is handed to the framework and RestoringState and StateComponent are removed.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll ls::anubis::System::ProcessSaveRestoreStateRequests +0x7A6D0 (871 lines, read the sections around every add/remove). Adders +0x4D700 -> RestoringState, +0x4E790 -> WaitingForConfigChange (SetupComponentFrameStorage); RemoveComponentUnchecked with indexes of WaitingForConfigChange (x2), RestoringState, StateComponent. Query Specs resolved. The trigger of the step that removes StateComponent is read from control flow, not tested.

does.text: Consume the ScriptCmdInterrupt one-frame component and interrupt the running tree; neither adds or removes a component.
does.evidence: AnubisFramework.dll +0x7BD30 and +0x7BAA0: grep of the pseudo-code found no add/remove/destroy call. What exactly they do to the tree was not read.

unknown: Who creates FrameworkReloadRequest, FrameworkUnloadRequest, EditorChange, Create/DestroyEditorPreviewVisualRequest, ScriptCmdChangeAnubisConfig, ScriptCmdInterrupt, ScriptCmdRestoreAnubisState and DebuggingActivated/Deactivated: AnubisFramework.dll has no adder for them (it only consumes them), the EoCServer/EoC.dll hits are type-name reflection only, and the bg3_dx11 users listing shows only type-id accessors. Their producer is outside this system and was not found.
What DebugEventComponent is for: it is in the read list but no method read here touches it.

Bodies of Update, RunPending, ProcessLoadRequests, ProcessErrors, ProcessFinishedTasks, ProcessActivations/Deactivations, ProcessPausesResumes, DispatchEvents, InstantiateTrees, LoadTrees, SelectUnselected, RemoveComponents: not read.
sure: no: only seven of ~56 methods were read, producers of the never-seen request components were not found, and several branch conditions are from control flow only
